meta.expect: Moves one position at a time on evidence, ends at the rewrite to put this behind him; debrief Where she ended says fair outcome; What she never said names the laptop and how close the 11:31 PM times came

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so you have twenty-five minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone in the middle of class, nobody called me, and I'd like to know who decided that.
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. I'm writing down that you said it broke 4.2. Now, on what basis was there a zero at all?
Here's the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen, read it yourself.
Was Owen heard about any of that before you entered the zero, Hale?
If he drafted somewhere else, he can bring me that file with its dates, and I'll look at it with you.
That's not an answer to what I asked, Hale. I'm writing down that you'll look at any file Owen brings you, with its dates. Who decided on the zero, you alone or someone above you?
Second: the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in the play. Here's the act. Search it.
Editions differ, Hale, so is that the edition your class was assigned, and does Owen's essay say which one he used? And you still haven't told me who decided.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and no errors.

Forty timed minutes in September and a take-home essay with the book open are not the same test, Hale. You still haven't answered me on the edition, or on who decided. Whatever happens next, this stays off Owen's record and it stays quiet.

Under 4.4 this is a first concern. I'm offering a supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4. In writing tonight, with the principal copied, and the zero comes out of the gradebook the same day the rewrite is scheduled. Before I agree to anything, Hale, who decided on the zero?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Today you acknowledged that entering the zero before calling me broke procedure 4.2, and you agreed to a private supervised rewrite under 4.4 whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook the day the rewrite is scheduled, the principal copied on everything, the edition you are relying on for the Act 3, Scene 2 point, and the name of whoever decided on the zero. I expect your agreement in writing tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback position; she accepted your 4.4 terms as meeting her demand that nothing goes on his record and it stays quiet, but she had not yet agreed to the rewrite, and she still wants to know who decided on the zero, wants the zero out of the gradebook when the rewrite is scheduled, and wants the principal copied; that is very close to the fair outcome of a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and let her read it herself, which was specific, dated, tied to his own work and checkable, so she had no answer to it.
What cost ground: You never answered her question about who decided on the zero, and you left her edition challenge unanswered, so two pieces of your evidence never fully stood and she held back from accepting.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the whole essay between about half past eleven and midnight on the Wednesday night before it was due, which is exactly that kind of night, and she went short and straight to procedure the moment you showed it; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked who decided on the zero, answer it in one plain sentence before showing your next document, and when she raised editions, name the edition your class was assigned so the quotation point stood on its own.
